name: Meshullam
overview: Meshullam was a male Levite and Aaronic priest known for his role during the public reading of the Law, where he stood on Ezra's left hand as the Scriptures were proclaimed. He is mentioned among the signatories of the sealed covenant document, indicating his participation in the religious reforms of his time. His priestly duties and tribal affiliation highlight his significant role in the post-exilic community.
namesAndTitles: The name Meshullam means 'restitution,' reflecting a Hebrew proper name without indication of divine origin. This meaning may subtly underscore themes of restoration present in the post-exilic period during which he served.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Meshullam explicitly as the son of Ginnethon, linking him to a known Levite family line. Beyond this, his descent from the tribe of Levi is affirmed, situating him within the priestly lineage essential to temple service.
scriptureSignificance: Meshullam's presence alongside Ezra during the public reading of the Law underscores his active participation in the religious revival and covenant renewal among the returned exiles. His inclusion among the signatories of the covenant document further attests to his commitment to upholding the Mosaic Law and priestly responsibilities. As an Aaronic priest, Meshullam contributed to the spiritual leadership necessary for reestablishing proper worship and obedience to God in Israel.
